t: This is 67 Holland Park, a building in Kensington and Chelsea. It's linked to Agnes Morton, an English tennis player who died here in 1952. She twice reached the ladies' singles final at Wimbledon, in 1908 and 1909. In 1914 she won the ladies' doubles there with her partner Elizabeth Ryan, and that same year she reached the singles final at the Northern Championships. She also finished fourth in ladies' lawn tennis at the 1908 Olympics. It's a quiet address now, but it belongs to the life of a notable sportswoman.
